avoid_supplements.name: Vitamin K supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Directly antagonizes warfarin's anticoagulant effect by serving as cofactor for clotting factor synthesis
avoid_supplements.action: Strictly avoid supplementation; maintain consistent dietary vitamin K intake instead

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors and potentiates anticoagulant effect
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplementation; monitor INR if patient takes >400 IU daily from food sources

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and may potentiate bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue use; counsel patient on bleeding risk if concurrent use unavoidable

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (concentrated/high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects and may increase bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplements; monitor INR closely if used

avoid_supplements.name: Cranberry supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May inhibit CYP2C9 and increase warfarin levels; procoagulant properties also reported
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplementation; advise patient to report if consuming cranberry products

caution_supplements.name: Fish oil (omega-3)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects at high doses; uncertain clinical significance
caution_supplements.action: Monitor INR; limit to <3g/day if concurrent use necessary

caution_supplements.name: CoQ10
caution_supplements.mechanism: Structurally similar to vitamin K; may reduce warfarin efficacy at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor INR; counsel on consistent intake and timing

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties; clinical significance unclear at culinary doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for bleeding; counsel on moderation

avoid_foods.name: High vitamin K foods (kale, spinach, collards, broccoli)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Vitamin K directly antagonizes warfarin effect; excessive intake reduces INR
avoid_foods.action: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake; do not eliminate but keep steady day-to-day

caution_foods.name: Cranberry juice/products
caution_foods.mechanism: May inhibit CYP2C9 and potentiate warfarin effect; evidence mixed
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; monitor INR if regular intake; advise consistency

caution_foods.name: Alcohol (especially heavy/binge use)
caution_foods.mechanism: Chronic use may induce CYP450; acute use may potentiate anticoagulant effect
caution_foods.action: Limit to ≤1-2 drinks/day; monitor INR with pattern changes

caution_foods.name: Avocado
caution_foods.mechanism: Contains small amounts of vitamin K; high intake may reduce warfarin efficacy
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption; maintain consistency; not necessary to eliminate

monitoring_notes: INR monitoring is essential with any dietary or supplement change; patient education on consistent vitamin K intake is critical since elimination and excessive intake both destabilize anticoagulation. Counsel patients to report all supplements and herbal products and to avoid sudden changes in dietary patterns.
